title: GPUs, tokens and fallbacks
summary: Serving AI answers is slow and expensive, so cache, limit, and have a fallback.

steps.title: Costly answers
steps.text: A chatbot answer needs a GPU, a chip that costs a few dollars an hour to rent (approx.) and can serve only a few conversations at once. Answers are measured in tokens, roughly three quarters of a word. Longer answers take longer and cost more, and the number of GPUs you can get is limited.

steps.prompt: A GPU shortage hits at noon. Add a fallback and remember repeated questions.
steps.hint: Place a Semantic cache in front of the model and a Hosted model API as a backup, with an LLM gateway to choose between them.

steps.title: Smaller and cached
steps.text: Many questions are the same or similar, so a semantic cache can answer from memory. A smaller model handles easy questions and a bigger one the hard ones. Limits on answer length keep cost predictable.

choices: Every answer is stored for years in a vault
A person has to read each answer first
Each answer keeps a costly GPU busy
The model is retrained for each user
steps.why: Each answer ties up a chip for seconds.

choices: Every single question is completely new
Many people ask nearly the same thing
The answers must differ every time
Nobody uses the system at all
steps.why: Similar questions can share one answer.

steps.q: What is a good plan for a GPU shortage?
choices: Wait until the shortage passes by itself
Delete the busiest GPUs to save power
Turn off the load balancer for a while
Fall back to a hosted or smaller model
steps.why: Serve degraded answers rather than none.

takeaway: Cache, cap and fall back; GPUs are the scarcest part of the system.
